Evidence Summary: Glean Agents execute multi-step workflows autonomously—retrieving information, executing code, and triggering actions across enterprise tools based on conversational, scheduled, trigger-based, or form inputs. Scheduled/background agents can run headless end-to-end without per-run user confirmation.
Evaluation Notes: Autonomous tool invocation and headless background runs are subject to administrator and agent-permission controls.

Evidence Summary: Glean's agentic planner breaks down complex goals using multi-stage prompting and prompt chaining, leveraging reasoning models (e.g., o3, Gemini Pro 2.5) to decide intermediate logic, select tools, and loop/branch until goal conditions are met.
Evaluation Notes: Supports reasoning-specific LLMs at both the overall agent level and individual step levels; adapts subsequent tool calls based on intermediate results.

Evidence Summary: Glean Agent Builder provides a visual flow canvas to define triggers, step sequences, document read actions, prompt formatting, loops, and conditional branching. Agents can also be auto-drafted from natural language and use planner-driven orchestration for multi-step execution and retries.
Evaluation Notes: Workflows support both visual step-by-step manual configuration and natural language generation.

Evidence Summary: Agents store inputs, outputs, conversation history, and prior step results in memory, leveraging Glean's Enterprise Graph and semantic RAG to persist and retrieve permission-aware context across connected company sources. Sub-agent outputs return directly to parent agent memory.
Evaluation Notes: Combines real-time step execution memory with enterprise-wide graph retrieval. Memory primarily persists execution context rather than cross-session user memory across unrelated runs.

Evidence Summary: Glean agents adapt dynamically during loops using tool feedback and intermediate results. Performance is continuously monitored via Agent Insights user feedback metrics (thumbs up/down), task-specific LLM judges, and evaluation test sets to guide prompt/step refinement.
Evaluation Notes: Evidence supports runtime loop adaptation and builder-driven prompt refinement based on analytics, but not autonomous continual model retraining from errors.

Evidence Summary: Glean supports Sub-agents as direct workflow steps (allowing parent agents to delegate tasks and ingest results) and enables agents to be exposed as callable tools over the Model Context Protocol (MCP) gateway for external multi-agent systems.
Evaluation Notes: MCP gateway compatibility enables standard agent-to-agent tool invocation across internal workflows and external agent platforms.

Evidence Summary: Glean Agent Builder provides a no-code visual canvas and a conversational "Build with Natural Language" interface that automatically generates workflow steps, triggers, and tool configurations from plain text descriptions.
Evaluation Notes: Users can visually reorder steps, add branching, and configure tool parameters; natural language drafting requires an agentic model configured in the org.

Evidence Summary: Glean's Model Hub supports commercial and open-source models from Anthropic (Claude), OpenAI (GPT-4, o3), Google (Gemini), Amazon, and Meta. Models can be configured globally, per agent, or independently for individual workflow steps.
Evaluation Notes: Allows granular, step-level assignment of specialized reasoning models versus standard generation models. Availability depends on hosting environment.

Evidence Summary: Features natural-language workflow generation, prebuilt agent templates, action integrations, prompt enhancement, live draft previewing, and an interactive step-by-step debug mode to inspect raw tool inputs, outputs, and data transformations.
Evaluation Notes: Interactive debug mode and prebuilt templates significantly reduce custom development overhead.

Evidence Summary: Glean provides 100+ native connectors (GitHub, Jira, Salesforce, Slack, Google Workspace, M365, Snowflake, Zendesk), standard REST APIs, and remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) server/gateway support to connect custom external tools.
Evaluation Notes: Exposes Glean enterprise knowledge and actions via both standard REST APIs and MCP interfaces (remote MCP noted in Beta).

Evidence Summary: Glean is available as a fully managed SaaS deployment or as Customer-Hosted Cloud-Prem in the customer's own AWS or GCP VPC environment, with support for private networking to on-prem data sources and AWS KMS Customer Managed Keys (CMK).
Evaluation Notes: Cloud-Prem provides isolated customer cloud deployment rather than a traditional bare-metal/on-premise package.

Evidence Summary: Glean enforces confirmation panels for write actions in interactive web sessions (allowing users to review, edit planned changes inline, approve, or cancel) and provides a dedicated "Wait for User Input" action for human confirmation workflows.
Evaluation Notes: Applied by default to interactive write actions to prevent accidental or unauthorized data modifications.

Evidence Summary: Glean provides agent run history, OpenTelemetry instrumentation, step-level debug traces of tool payloads, deep-linked citations linking directly back to source documents, and an Agent Insights dashboard tracking adoption and user feedback.
Evaluation Notes: Strong operational observability and deep-linked source attribution; does not represent formal model feature-attribution explainability.

Evidence Summary: Features real-time enterprise permission mirroring (document-level ACLs), RBAC, SSO, administrator roles, audit logs, DLP policy enforcement, content-hiding APIs, SOC 2 Type II compliance, and granular publishing/background execution controls.
Evaluation Notes: Strict identity, access control, and automated governance violation enforcement across all integrated enterprise data.

Evidence Summary: Glean scales automatically across SaaS and isolated Cloud-Prem environments, processing petabyte-scale search and agent workloads using distributed indexing, KV cache optimization for latency, and scalable MCP architectures (e.g., 3,400+ agents deployed at Zillow).
Evaluation Notes: Verified enterprise adoption supporting thousands of concurrent users and agents across large-scale corp infrastructures.

Evidence Summary: Glean provides pre-built workflows and action packs across HR, IT service management, software engineering, finance, legal/contracts, recruiting, customer support, and sales ops (with deployments at Zillow, Duolingo, DNI, and McCarthy).
Source Type: Customer case studies and implementation stories
Evaluation Notes: Broad cross-industry coverage with specialized workflows for code search, ticket deflection, and CRM management.

Evidence Summary: A Forrester Total Economic Impact study found a 141% three-year ROI, payback in under 6 months, and $26.6M in total benefits for a 10k-employee firm (saving up to 110 hrs/employee annually); Duolingo reported a 5x ROI and $1.1M in annual time savings.
Evaluation Notes: Demonstrates substantial productivity and time-saving gains; Forrester study was commissioned by Glean and customer metrics are self-reported.
